text.paragraph: New patient visit for three months of low mood, exhaustion, poor sleep and withdrawal: depression screening, safety assessment and safety plan, tests for medical causes, and urgent psychiatric consultation. Concerns: He is exhausted, sleeps poorly and has lost the wish to sing, and wants to know what is wrong; He worries that a psychiatric record could be used against him by the people who have taken his passport and his work; He wants to keep working for civil rights and to sing again. [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for three months of low mood, exhaustion, poor sleep and withdrawal: depression screening, safety assessment and safety plan, tests for medical causes, and urgent psychiatric consultation
Psychiatric consultation and review: diagnosis of recurrent major depression, bipolar screening, start of sertraline and behavioral activation
Six-week review: minimal response; sertraline increased
Three-month review: no response to an adequate sertraline trial; switch to venlafaxine
Twenty-four-week review: partial response to venlafaxine; treatment-resistant depression; aripiprazole augmentation and an informed consent discussion about ECT
Same-day sick visit for acute bronchitis on venlafaxine

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Evaluation: PHQ-9, GAD-7, AUDIT-C and a cognitive screen (MoCA); blood count, metabolic panel, calcium, TSH, vitamin B12, folate, morning testosterone and hemoglobin A1c, with HIV and syphilis tests, to exclude medical causes; a review of medicines; and a sleep apnea screen

Urgent psychiatric consultation in three days to confirm the diagnosis with a structured interview, screen for bipolar disorder, judge suicide risk and the level of care, and advise on psychotherapy, medicines, and when ECT or other treatments would be indicated

Safety: structured suicide-risk assessment, a written safety plan, no firearm in the home, medicines dispensed in limited supplies and kept locked, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and a safety review at every visit

Trust and equity: explain who can see his record and how it is protected; a therapist of his choosing, including a Black clinician if he wishes; treat discrimination and persecution as real stressors and record his account of surveillance as realistic; a social worker for help with income and costs; guard against the documented under-treatment of depression in Black patients by measuring response at every visit

Treatment: behavioral activation weekly with a psychologist for about sixteen sessions, then CBT if needed; sertraline 50 mg, raised to 100 mg at two weeks and to 200 mg by eight weeks as tolerated; PHQ-9 at every visit with response defined as a 50 percent fall and remission as a score below 5; sodium at about six weeks; switch to an SNRI if the PHQ-9 falls by less than a quarter after an adequate trial, and consider augmentation, ECT, rTMS or esketamine if a second adequate trial brings only a partial response; watch for hypomania after starting an antidepressant

Switch to venlafaxine extended-release by cross-taper: venlafaxine 75 mg for a week while sertraline is halved, then 150 mg for three weeks and 225 mg; blood pressure at every visit; 30-day supplies because venlafaxine is more dangerous in overdose

Treatment-resistant depression: aripiprazole 2 mg, raised to 5 mg at two weeks, with weight at four, eight and twelve weeks, A1c and lipids at baseline and twelve weeks, and an abnormal involuntary movement examination at baseline and six months; an informed consent discussion about ECT (general anesthesia with a muscle relaxant, right unilateral ultrabrief pulse, two or three treatments a week in a defined course, cognitive testing before and during the course, and the right to stop at any time), with rTMS and esketamine as alternatives; ECT not started now and offered if augmentation fails or if he becomes unable to eat or drink, psychotic or acutely suicidal
GL-VADOD-MDD-2022, GL-APA-DEP-2019, GL-APA-ECT-2001, GL-APA-ECT-2024, GL-SPRENGER-2025, GL-CMID-2026

Acute bronchitis: no antibiotic and no chest X-ray with normal vital signs and a normal chest examination; honey, warm drinks and steam; plain guaifenesin if needed; no dextromethorphan, which with venlafaxine can cause serotonin syndrome, and no pseudoephedrine or phenylephrine, which raise blood pressure further on venlafaxine; check labels of combination cold remedies; return for fever, breathlessness, chest pain or a cough lasting more than three weeks

Prevention: stool FIT kit for colorectal screening; the earlier prostate surgery records obtained before any decision on PSA testing; a ten-year cardiovascular risk of about 9 percent discussed, with his choice of diet and activity first and a statin to be reconsidered in a year; hepatitis B and C screening; influenza, PCV20 and the first recombinant zoster dose today, the second zoster dose in two to six months
Response to treatment: PHQ-9 down by at least half from 22
PHQ-9 6 at about seven months, a 73 percent fall
Not yet met: PHQ-9 6 six weeks after augmentation; continuing
Stay safe: safety plan in place and reviewed at every visit, with no self-harm
Met so far: no thoughts of suicide since the first months; safety plan reviewed at every visit
Sing again: daily vocal practice and one public engagement a month
Daily practice resumed; sang at two community gatherings in the past month
Sleep six to seven hours a night
About six and a half hours a night

list.item: Independent in daily activities; has stopped practicing and performing, reads little, and has turned down invitations to speak over the past two months [S]

Tall, courteous and dignified; slowed movements and a quiet voice; mood 'worn through'; constricted affect; thought logical and goal-directed; no delusions or hallucinations; his account of being watched is consistent with the documented surveillance and is not treated as paranoia; insight and judgment good [S]
PHQ-9 22 with item 9 scored 1: thoughts on several days that he would be better off dead, without intent or plan; no past suicide attempt; GAD-7 12; MoCA 28 [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1957-03-09: current ideation present, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with a psychiatric consultation in three days and close follow-up. C-SSRS screen: wish to be dead on several days in the past month; no active thoughts of suicide, intent, plan, preparation or past attempt. Risk factors reviewed: severe depression, an older man, insomnia, loss of work and income, isolation, and sustained persecution. Means counseling: there is no firearm in the home and he will not acquire one; medicines will be dispensed in limited supplies and kept in a locked box. A written safety plan was made with him, with warning signs, coping steps, people and places for distraction, and crisis numbers; the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was saved in his phone. Safety is reviewed at every visit [S]
